items.text: Patients cannot book or move an appointment outside opening hours, and the front desk spends hours on the phone.

Patients pay a **$50 deposit by card at booking** for any service of **$150 or more**. The rest is paid after the visit by card, Interac e-Transfer, or cash. (Who pays to run the app, and how the deposit is handled, are open questions below.)

items.section: The users, and what each may do
items.text: **Owner (me)** — everything, including approving refunds.
items.comment: Also log the reason for every refund.

items.section: The users, and what each may do
items.text: **Location manager** (one per location) — staff, hours, and reports for their own location.

items.section: The users, and what each may do
items.text: **Front desk** — bookings, payments, and cash for their own location.

items.section: The users, and what each may do
items.text: **Practitioner** — their own calendar and their own patients' notes.

items.section: The users, and what each may do
items.text: **Patient** — their own bookings and payments.

items.section: The users, and what each may do
items.text: **AI receptionist** — reads `hello@nextiaclinic.com` and the website chat; answers from clinic policies; books and moves appointments. It never gives medical advice, never sees medical notes, only *proposes* refunds, and hands off to the front desk when it is not sure.
The app keeps names, contact details, appointments, payments, and health information. **Health information is the most sensitive.**
A $50 card deposit is taken at booking for any service of $150 or more.
The remainder is paid after the visit by card, Interac e-Transfer, or cash.
Cancelling is free up to **24 hours before** the appointment. Cancelling later than that (including a no-show) means the **deposit is kept**.
items.comment: 24 hours before the appointment, not one day before the date

items.text: Only the **owner** can approve a refund. The AI receptionist can only *propose* one.
Every payment change is logged with **who did it and when**.
Staff (location manager and front desk) act within **their own location** only.
Practitioners see only **their own** calendar and their own patients' notes.
A double booking.
A patient seeing another patient's record.
A refund to the wrong person.
A phone app in the app stores.
Billing to insurance companies.
Video visits.
Other clinics using the app.

items.section: How we will know it works
items.text: Fewer phone calls to the front desk.

items.section: How we will know it works
items.text: Fewer missed appointments.

**Deposit applied to the bill** — When the patient attends, is the $50 deposit applied to the final bill, or kept separately? *(The cancel/no-show rule is now decided: free up to 24 hours before, deposit kept after that.)*
**Who pays to run the app** — Who covers hosting, email, payments, and AI model costs?
**Full data model and sensitivity** — Confirmed so far: names, contact details, appointments, payments, health information. Any other data to store, and how each is classified?
**Children / minors** — Does the clinic treat minors, and must the app handle guardian/parental consent and access?

**Which laws apply** — Not yet decided. Candidates to confirm with a professional (see `checklists/rules-that-apply.md`): federal PIPEDA, Quebec Law 25, Ontario PHIPA, and French-language rules (OQLF). *The English/French requirement itself is decided and firm.*
**Monthly budget** — Total monthly budget for the agent, hosting, email, payments, and AI model, so a budget alert can be set on every paid service.
